title: Pisa Device Protocol v1
description: Messages exchanged over the device WebSocket (/v1/device). Shared contract between Pisa Core and every device app. See protocol/README.md.

object_id.description: An object Pisa showed: '<kind or Pisa's own record>:<id>' (plan:2026-10-28, task:<uuid>, event:<calendar>/<id>, compare:<uuid>…). The same object keeps its id when Pisa shows it again (revision grows).

focus_mode.description: take: bring it in front now (the device may defer it while the user reads or edits); offer: a chip one tap away; quiet: into the history only.

present.description: Pisa -> device (only to a device whose hello.capabilities.present lists object.kind). Show one object. ref: what Pisa holds (plan, item, changes, setting, place): the device reads it through the REST it already uses, so the object is the truth, not a copy. data: only what the turn computed (places, compare, note, choice). Showing never changes anything. The device answers presented with the same present_id at once (Pisa waits at most 800 ms).

reply_to.description: The utterance this answers, or null when Pisa shows it unasked.

agenda.description: No plan is stored for that day: show its agenda (GET /v1/agenda?from=<date>&days=1); absent = false

data.description: 2-4 places side by side; each row's cells follow criteria in order. Every cell comes from the turn's own tool results; an unchecked one is unknown.
A question answerable by tap or voice; a tap comes back as object_event chosen with its option_id.

A sheet Pisa composes, each block in the app's own fixed template (never a page's HTML; a phone skips a block type it doesn't know). Images and links: https, from the pages Pisa read this turn (or a place's photos); at most 6 images; 24 blocks.

oneOf.description: A heading that opens a part of the sheet.
Every row as long as the columns; cells are text or numbers.

What Pisa prepared behind one big button; the phone opens url (or dials phone) in the official app and sends handoff_opened. Built by Pisa from its own templates: https, tel:+<E.164> (the same number as phone) or sms:[+<E.164>]&body=<encoded>; never javascript:, data:, file: or any other scheme.

actions.description: Pisa's buttons on a ritual's sheet (only code makes them; never a composed sheet). The app posts POST /v1/sheets/{id}/actions/{action_id}.

data.description: A page Pisa wrote (HTML, inline SVG, inline JavaScript), checked on the server before it is sent (size, it parses, no address, no network, storage, form, frame or navigation, no markup written from values, nothing that looks like Pisa's approval) and sealed: Pisa put a strict CSP (default-src 'none', each inline script allowed by its sha256 hash and never 'unsafe-inline', form-action 'none', base-uri 'none') as the first meta of the page, before anything it runs. The check is defence in depth; the phone's box is the wall: a web view with no network (every load blocked but the page and the bundled libraries), no storage, no cookies, no device access, no navigation. The page reads `data` as window.PISA_DATA. Its only way out is 'ask Pisa about this' (drawing.ask), after his tap; its label is the page's text (quarantined by Pisa). summary: for VoiceOver. basis 'knowledge': Pisa drew what it knows (no data fetched this turn), captioned 'Da quello che so'.

libraries.description: The bundled libraries the page loads as <script src="pisa-bundle://lib/<name>.min.js">, with the app's pinned version: the app serves them from its own bundle (d3 7.9.0, mermaid 12.2.0, vega 6.4.0, vega-lite 6.5.0, vega-embed 7.3.0, vega-interpreter 2.3.2).

purpose.description: What the user gets from seeing it, in their language (the model's words; for the screen, never for a log).

highlight.description: A part to point at: an item's id or title, a setting's key, an option id.

presented.description: device -> Pisa. The acknowledgment of a present or focus (same present_id), sent at once: shown (in front), queued (the app is in the background: there when the user opens Pisa), deferred (the user is reading or editing: an unseen dot), unavailable (no screen on the surface in use, e.g. glasses only), unsupported (a kind this app can't show). Pisa says in words what wasn't shown.

object_event.description: device -> Pisa. What the user did with an object: seen (on screen 2 s or more with the app in front), expanded, kept (pinned), closed, chosen (a choice's option: option_id; it becomes the user's own message), acted (an action on it: action). Ids only: never gaze, never content.

drawing_ask.description: Device -> Pisa: 'ask Pisa about this', after the user's tap on a drawing Pisa showed. label: the page's text (an element's data-pisa-ask value, or what the page passed to Pisa.ask), 1-120 user-perceived characters (grapheme clusters; this schema caps code points at 960): Pisa treats it as outside text, quarantined, grounding nothing. Pisa answers it as his turn marked as coming from the drawing ('Sul disegno: <label>'): it may read and answer, never approve, send or change anything. Pisa's reply (say) answers this message's id; an unknown drawing, or a second ask within 2 s, gets an error with reply_to.

focus.description: Pisa -> device. Bring an object Pisa already showed back in front, or point at a part of it (highlight). Acknowledged with presented (same present_id).

close.description: Pisa -> device. Take an object off the screen (it stays in the history). No acknowledgment.

hello.description: device -> Pisa. First message after the socket opens. Pisa answers with welcome or error(auth_failed | protocol_version_unsupported).

audio_formats.description: Formats of Pisa's voice (say_audio) the device can play. Absent or empty: Pisa sends no audio and the device speaks the text itself.

present.description: The device shows Pisa's objects (present, focus, close) and acknowledges them (presented, object_event). kinds: the object kinds it can show; focus: it honours take/offer/quiet. Absent: Pisa sends today's card messages instead (the fallback); a kind not listed gets no present (Pisa says it in words).

kinds.description: The object kinds this app shows. Any string: Pisa keeps the kinds it knows (object_kind) and logs the rest, so a newer app's hello never fails on an older Pisa.

wearable.description: Connected wearable, if any (e.g. Meta glasses via DAT).

turn_hints.description: The app will send partial transcripts (utterance with final false, at most 2 a second, only while listening) and wants a turn_hint back for each one Pisa scores. Absent or false: Pisa ignores partials.

tz.description: The phone's IANA time zone (TimeZone.current.identifier). A zone Pisa can't load keeps the last known.

hour_cycle.description: How the user reads times: h23 (15:00) or h12 (3:00 PM).

device_context.description: Device -> Pisa: the phone's zone, region or hour cycle changed while the socket is open (a landing, a settings change). At least one field. Pisa answers nothing; absent fields keep the last known.

handoff_opened.description: Device -> Pisa: the user tapped a handoff's button and its URL opened (the official app now has his yes to give). Pisa answers nothing; only the first open counts; an unknown id is dropped.

utterance.description: device -> Pisa. What the user said, already transcribed on the device. Only final=true utterances are acted on. final=false is a partial transcript: sent only after a hello with turn_hints true, at most 2 a second, only while listening; Pisa answers the ones it scores with turn_hint, never starts a reply from one and never stores or logs its words.

wake.description: How this turn started: the wake phrase, an earbud press, a tap, or an answer to a notify with expects_reply.

continues.description: The user went on talking after Pisa closed the turn. The id of the earlier final utterance this one continues: Pisa cancels that one's reply (if still running) and answers the joined words as one turn, the earlier words first.

voice.description: How the user spoke this turn, each field measured on the phone against HIS OWN rolling 30-day baseline, which stays on the phone (never synced, never sent). Observables only: never an emotion. Optional: absent on old builds, on typed turns, and for any field the phone could not measure.

say.description: Pisa -> device. A reply, streamed in chunks. All chunks of one reply share stream_id; seq starts at 0; the last chunk has final=true (its delta may be empty).

holding.description: A holding phrase Pisa says when the answer isn't ready ~700 ms after the utterance arrived. The app plays it from its cache (holding_id, from protocol/holding-phrases.v1.json); no say_audio comes for it. The answer follows in the same stream.

holding_id.description: With holding: true, one id of protocol/holding-phrases.v1.json (it/en, at most 4 words).

turn_hint.description: Pisa -> device, within 150 ms of a partial utterance Pisa scored: how likely the user has finished (p_end, 0 to 1) and how long the app should wait at this pause before closing the turn (wait_ms). Today both come from the word rules, the shared table protocol/turn-rules.v1.json (unfinished words: 0 and 3000; a complete question or command: 1 and 1200; otherwise 0.5 and 1800); a model may replace the rules later, so the app follows wait_ms, never its own reading of p_end. A later partial's hint replaces an earlier one.

understood.description: Pisa -> device, before Pisa's answer to an utterance: what Pisa understood the user meant, sent only when something changed (a filler, a repair, a name) or Pisa asks a question. The phone shows `meant` with each correction's `to` underlined; `raw` is what the recogniser wrote. `via`: sound or spelling (fixed by rules), model (the small model decided: Pisa also says the name back). `ask`: Pisa's one short question (two names alike, a contradiction of hour, day or city), which is then Pisa's whole answer.

place_enter.description: device -> Pisa. The phone entered the regions of these place notes (or of open tasks with a place: task:<uuid>). Pisa answers with the note (a notify), once a visit (6 h).

location.description: device -> Pisa. Position update (sent on significant change, at most every 30 s while moving).

card.description: Pisa -> device. Something to show on a screen (phone, glasses display). Devices without display ignore it. kind=place carries place_id: the app opens that place's card (GET /v1/places/{id}). kind=places (show_places) carries request and places: the best 1 to 3 places Pisa found, each with why it fits and each requirement as checked (verified / likely / unknown / no, with its source); lines then hold one line per place for a display without the places view. kind=sources carries sources: the links behind a web answer; lines then hold one line per link.

photo_count.description: GET /v1/places/{id}/details lists them; /photos/{index} gives each URL

closes_at.description: RFC 3339, when open now and known

opens_at.description: RFC 3339, when closed now and known

fits.description: what in the user's taste it matches

different.description: something different: unlike the user's usual, shown with a label; at most one place per card, about 1 card in 5; `why` says how it differs

sources.description: kind=sources: the pages behind a web answer, sent with every one (the pages this turn's searches returned, those it read first). The app opens each link in Safari and shows its host.

notify.description: Pisa -> device. A proactive message (reminder, briefing, check-in, done). The device speaks it if a wearable (glasses, or earbuds in companion mode) is connected and quiet mode is off, otherwise shows it. kind=check_in carries check_in_id and choices: the device shows them as buttons and, with expects_reply, listens for a spoken answer right after speaking (no wake phrase needed). kind=done says Pisa closed a task or marked today's event attended because the user stayed at its place 10 minutes (or said so): a banner with Undo until undo_until; the task leaves Today at once.

weekly.description: kind=info: the weekly check is ready (GET /v1/profile/weekly); the app opens its card

ledger_week.description: kind=info: the Sunday card of this ISO week is ready (GET /v1/ledger/summary?week=); the app opens its sheet

event_id.description: kind=done: today's event Pisa marked attended (POST /v1/events/{id}/undo-attended)

title.description: kind=done: the task's or event's title

place.description: kind=done: where the user was; absent at a sensitive place or when the user said it

undo_until.description: kind=done: Undo works until then (24 h)

urgency.description: Pisa speaking first. now (time- or safety-critical: leave now, an event within 10 minutes, an alert): the app says it after the current sentence; its text opens with "Scusa, un attimo:". breakpoint: the app queues it for the end of the exchange; Pisa itself holds it while the user talks to Pisa and during a meeting. The user's "dopo" right after it puts it off once (Pisa answers "Ok, dopo." and sends it again at the next breakpoint).

voice.description: False = show it (a banner or the notice), don't speak it: Pisa's unprompted voice rate (3 an hour, 12 a day) was reached; no say_audio follows. Absent: as today (the app speaks it in companion mode with earbuds or with the glasses on). Leaving now and an event about to start always come without it.

ritual.description: A ritual's notice (kind info); with sheet_id, a tap opens that sheet (GET /v1/sheets/{sheet_id}). People, an offer about someone he loves (a moment, a thank-you, a wish) whose sheet holds handoff buttons with Pisa's draft. Stanotte, on the morning briefing's notice (kind briefing): its sheet is last night's

sheet_id.description: The ritual's sheet, a view sheet with Pisa's buttons

talk_ask_to_open.description: Pisa -> device. Pisa has something to say first and no talk is open: the phone opens a talk with trigger proactive and ask_id = this message's id, and Pisa says line first (only within 10 minutes of this message; later it is an ordinary talk); when it can't open one, it shows line as a time-sensitive notification whose action opens that talk. notification_id is the item's own notify, which comes with voice false: the phone shows one alert, not two.

say_audio.description: Pisa -> device. Pisa's spoken voice: audio for a reply (stream_id, the same as its say chunks) or for a notify (notification_id), in seq order, the last with final=true. Base64 in data. The device plays it instead of speaking the text itself; if the first chunk is late (1.5 s after the text) or never comes, it speaks the text with its own voice. A cancel of the reply stops these too.

sentence_end.description: true on a chunk whose audio ends a sentence of the reply (not needed on the final chunk). A device that interrupts or ducks the voice may stop at the next chunk marked so. Absent means unknown: no boundary is promised.

complete.description: On the final chunk: false when the audio stopped early (a provider error); the device then speaks the reply's text from spoken_chars on with its own voice.

spoken_chars.description: On a final chunk with complete=false: how many characters of the reply's text the audio covered: the say deltas each trimmed of surrounding whitespace, empty ones dropped, joined with one space, counted in Unicode code points.

compose.description: Pisa -> device. A message for the user to send from the phone: the device resolves the recipient in its contacts and opens the compose screen (foreground, after a confirmation) or a notification that opens it when tapped. The user's own tap on Send is the approval.

call.description: Pisa -> device. Call a place or a person: the device dials after a confirmation (foreground) or offers it in a notification.

directions.description: Pisa -> device. Open turn-by-turn directions to a place in the phone's maps app ("portami a..."). In the foreground the app opens Apple Maps at once; in the background it shows a notification that opens them when tapped (iOS lets no app open another from the background).

approval_request.description: Pisa -> device. An R2 action waiting for the user's yes/no. In companion mode the device speaks the summary and listens 8 s for si/no; otherwise it shows Approve / Reject (Face ID when requires_biometric).

undo_minutes.description: 1440 (24 h) for calendar kinds; null for email_send (a sent email can't be undone).

action_done.description: Pisa -> device. Pisa changed something on the user's own words with no question (or right after their spoken yes): the app shows the result with Undo until undo_until (absent when it can't be undone) and lists it under Changes. POST /v1/approvals/{approval_id}/undo undoes it.

approval_response.description: device -> Pisa. The user's decision. auth=biometric is required when requires_biometric was true.

cancel.description: device -> Pisa. The user interrupted (barge-in or 'stop'). Pisa stops streaming that reply.

presence.description: device -> Pisa. The user just became reachable or stopped being reachable on this device. glasses_on/glasses_off come from the glasses' wear (don) sensor; app_foreground/app_background from the app lifecycle. Pisa uses them for event-triggered briefings. Send on change only, plus the current state right after welcome.

state.description: Optional: the device's whole current state with this event, so Pisa knows where its words land (the body line). A lock or audio-route change re-sends the current app_foreground/app_background with the new state.

error.description: Either direction. code is machine-readable (closed list below); message says the real cause in plain words; action says what to do.
